    • FX MORNING NOTES

    GS FX Research Notes: European Risk Collisions, Payrolls Coming Up

    Research | Economics | 2 October 2026 | 8:40AM UTC

    Euro. Despite seemingly limited fundamental developments on the European fiscal front yesterday, fluctuations and stress in sovereign credit drove much of the price action in the Euro and European assets (first chart below). The push through 17-month lows in EUR/USD and positioning unwinds in key Euro crosses likely accelerated these moves, adding a clear technical element, and helping define the overall shape of the FX imprint. Relative to their historical betas to shifting OAT-Bund spreads, most Euro crosses saw outsized downside pressures yesterday, but this was clearest in EUR/NOK, EUR/SEK, and EUR/CHF (second chart below). Unwinds in Swiss Franc funding positions likely played a key role there, but we think the OAT-led widening in Euro credit spreads occurring against a broader backdrop of surprisingly resilient European growth outcomes has helped keep some of the high-beta Euro satellites more insulated than the empirical sensitivities would imply.

    Payrolls. The past four months of jobs reports have all generated meaningful initial reactions in the broad Dollar and front-end rates (third chart below). We think the higher-than-usual volatility in the jobs growth data itself have been a key contributor to that (fourth chart below), in spite of the lower emphasis currently placed on labor market data versus inflation data by many Fed officials. That has been especially true for quantity-based measures (including headline jobs growth) relative to ratios (including many measures of slack), and our economists’ trackers point to divergence between these two types of measures in recent months. Recent alternative data on jobs growth have improved, supporting expectations for a firmer NFP print today, while our economists’ slack tracker has moderated.

    Charts of the Day: European macro assets largely fluctuated in tandem yesterday, led by widening, spillovers, and stress in European sovereign credit.

    Relative to their historical betas to shifting OAT-Bund spreads, most Euro crosses saw outsized downside pressures yesterday. This was clearest in outperformance in some of the Euro’s satellites (particularly NOK, SEK, CHF), while the EUR/USD and broad Dollar reactions were both more consistent with historical sensitivities.

     

    The past four jobs reports have all generated meaningful initial broad Dollar reactions. 

    Both surprises to consensus and the variation across jobs growth prints have been larger so far in 2026 than on average in each of the past three years.
